booting.text: FX desk — give me a moment, the board is still warming up.

no_account.text: Dollars to euros or shekels, or back again? I'd love to, but I trade out of your account, not out of my pocket. Iris opens one at Account Opening.

why_account.text: Every trade here is executed by your own account contract, on the exchange's terms and under your guard list. Until that contract exists there is nothing for the router to talk to.

desk_closed.text: Board's dark today — the branch can't reach the exchange floor. Counter and the vault are unaffected.

why_desk_closed.text: {fx_chain_note} When that side isn't configured or won't answer, I close the board rather than quote you a price I can't honour.

no_till.text: You've no till on the exchange floor yet. I can open one — {fx_till_note}.

choices.working: Opening your till and setting up the exchange desk…

why_till.text: Your FX till is {fx_till_note}. Same owner, same tellers, same rules — and either way the exchange itself is on Sepolia, because that is where the pools are.

closed_door.text: Till's there, but the exchange isn't fully on your approved list yet — the three exchange services, each currency you might sell, and euros and shekels on the counter's list too. I can't trade until the manager's list says so.

opened.text: Done. Your account may now prepare a payment in dollars, euros or shekels, authorise the exchange, and place the trade — both ways. And what you hold in euros or shekels can go out over Eve's counter, same as dollars. {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in}, {fx_eur} EUR and {fx_ils} ILS in the till.

whitelist.text: Three services on the exchange side — prepare the currency you're selling, authorise the exchange, place the trade — in dollars, euros or shekels, either direction. Plus the counter: euros and shekels you hold here can be paid out by Eve, same as dollars. That list is on your account, not my desk — I couldn't send your money anywhere else if you asked me to. No euro-to-shekel, and no fiat through the vault.

why_swap.text: Your account calls the exchange router directly, but only because that router is on your approved list for that exact function. Same guard as payments. Euros and shekels are two pools behind one door, and each pool trades both ways.

why_guard.text: GuardController holds a whitelist per function selector. Your till registered three schemas — approve(address,uint256), Permit2's approve, and execute(bytes,bytes[],uint256) — and whitelisted the dollar, the euro and the shekel for the first, one address for each of the others. The counter's own transfer(address,uint256) gained the euro and the shekel as targets. You sign a meta-transaction, the FX teller submits it, and the account refuses any target that is not on that list. A swap is a treasury operation here, not a wallet pop-up.

why_quote.text: The board is the exchange's own quoter, asked off-chain — it costs nothing and signs nothing. Each currency has its own pool, a hundred million deep, so a desk-sized order barely moves the rate whichever way you trade. I take one percent off the quote as your floor, stamp a five-minute deadline, and the router refuses the trade if the pool has moved past that floor by the time it lands.
